title: Printers and printing
monthTitle: PC Hardware & How Computers Work (A+ Core 1)
summary: Learn the main printer types and how laser printing works, then connect, manage, and troubleshoot printers like a helpdesk technician using Windows tools and PowerShell.
objectives: Explain the differences between inkjet, laser, thermal, and 3D printers
Describe the seven steps of the laser printing process at a high level
Connect a printer over USB, network IP, wireless, or as a shared printer
Explain the role of printer drivers and the Windows print spooler
Troubleshoot common faults like paper jams, streaks, stuck spoolers, and offline printers
Identify the right consumables: toner for laser, ink for inkjet

quiz.q: Which printer type uses a laser, a charged drum, and heat to fuse toner onto paper?
quiz.why: A laser printer charges a drum, uses a laser to write the image, attracts powdered toner, then fuses it to the paper with heat and pressure. Inkjets spray liquid ink instead.

quiz.q: A user reports their printer shows as 'Offline' even though it is powered on. What is a sensible FIRST check?
options: Check the cable or network connection and that the printer is set as default
quiz.why: Offline usually means Windows cannot reach the printer. Check the USB cable or network/Wi-Fi connection first before touching consumables or doing anything drastic.

quiz.q: What does the Windows print spooler service do?
options: It fuses toner to the paper
It manages and queues print jobs being sent to printers
It scans documents into the computer
quiz.why: The spooler (Spooler service) accepts print jobs, queues them, and feeds them to the printer in order. If it gets stuck, restarting the service clears the jam.

quiz.q: Which command lists the printers installed on a Windows machine?
quiz.why: Get-Printer is the PowerShell cmdlet that returns the installed printers and their status, a quick first step when diagnosing printing problems.

quiz.q: In one sentence, what is the difference between toner and ink?
quiz.answer: Toner is the dry powder used by laser printers and fused with heat, while ink is the liquid used by inkjet printers and sprayed onto the page.
quiz.why: Knowing which consumable a printer uses tells you what to order and what causes faults: dry toner streaks versus wet ink smudges or clogged nozzles.

quiz.q: A print job is stuck in the queue and nothing prints. Name a PowerShell command that often fixes this.
quiz.answer: Restart-Service -Name Spooler (after optionally clearing stuck jobs with Get-PrintJob / Remove-PrintJob).
quiz.why: Restarting the Spooler service clears a hung queue so jobs can flow again; it is one of the most common helpdesk printing fixes.

resources.label: Microsoft Support — Fix printer connection and printing problems in Windows

body_markdown:
## Printer types you'll meet on the helpdesk

Most printers fall into a few families. An **inkjet** printer sprays tiny droplets of liquid **ink** onto the page; they are cheap to buy, great for photos, but the ink can smudge and nozzles clog if unused. A **laser** printer uses a laser, a drum, and powdered **toner** fused with heat; they are fast, sharp for text, and cheaper per page in busy offices. A **thermal** printer uses heat to darken special paper or melt a ribbon and is common for **receipts, labels, and shipping**. A **3D** printer is a different beast entirely: it builds physical objects layer by layer from melted plastic filament. As a Tier 1 tech, you'll spend most of your time on laser and inkjet office printers.

## How a laser printer actually works

Laser printing follows **seven steps** in order. You don't need to memorise the physics, but knowing the sequence helps you locate a fault:

1. **Processing** — the printer receives the job and builds the page image in memory.
2. **Charging** — a uniform negative charge is applied to the rotating drum.
3. **Exposing** — the laser writes the image by discharging spots on the drum.
4. **Developing** — toner sticks to the discharged areas, forming the image.
5. **Transferring** — the toner image is moved onto the paper.
6. **Fusing** — heat and pressure melt the toner so it bonds permanently.
7. **Cleaning** — leftover toner and charge are wiped so the drum is ready again.

A repeating mark or **streak** down every page often points to a damaged drum or dirty fuser.

## Connecting printers

There are four common connection methods. **USB** is a direct cable to one PC — simplest, but only that PC can print. **Network / IP** printers sit on the LAN with their own **I P address**, so anyone on the network can reach them. **Wireless (Wi-Fi)** printers join the network without a cable. A **shared** printer is one PC's local printer that it shares out to others. For network printers, knowing the IP lets you browse to the printer's web page or add it directly.

## Drivers and the print spooler

Windows needs a **driver** — software that translates documents into the printer's language. The **print spooler** is a Windows service that accepts jobs, queues them, and feeds them to the printer one at a time. When printing breaks, these two are the usual suspects. List printers and the queue with PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-Printer
Get-PrintJob -PrinterName "Office-Laser"
```

## Common issues and quick fixes

**Paper jams** — power off, gently remove paper in the direction of travel, check for torn scraps. **Streaks or faded print** — low or faulty toner/ink, or a dirty drum. **Stuck spooler** — jobs pile up and nothing prints; clear the queue and restart the service. **Offline printer** — Windows can't reach it; check the cable, Wi-Fi, or IP, and confirm it's the default printer. To clear a hung queue:

```powershell
Get-PrintJob -PrinterName "Office-Laser" | Remove-PrintJob
Restart-Service -Name Spooler
```

## Consumables

Match the supply to the printer: **laser printers use toner cartridges** (dry powder), **inkjets use ink cartridges or tanks** (liquid). Ordering the wrong one is a common Tier 1 mistake. Always note the exact model number before ordering.

## Your task

On a Windows PC, open PowerShell and run `Get-Printer` to list the installed printers. Pick one, run `Get-PrintJob -PrinterName "<name>"` to view its queue, then practise restarting the spooler with `Restart-Service -Name Spooler`. Write down the printer's connection type (USB, network IP, or wireless) and whether it uses toner or ink.

slides.narration: Welcome to Lesson Eight. Printers are one of the most common things you'll support on a helpdesk, and they break in very predictable ways. In this lesson you'll learn the main printer types, how laser printing actually works, how printers connect, and how to fix the everyday faults like jams, streaks, and a stuck print queue.

slides.title: The main printer types
bullets: Inkjet: sprays liquid ink, great for photos.
Laser: uses toner and heat, fast and sharp.
Thermal: heat-based, used for receipts and labels.
3D: builds objects layer by layer.
slides.narration: Let's meet the family. An inkjet printer sprays tiny droplets of liquid ink, and it's great for photos but can smudge. A laser printer uses powdered toner fused with heat; it's fast and sharp for text. A thermal printer uses heat for receipts and labels. And a three D printer is completely different, building physical objects layer by layer. On the helpdesk you'll mostly deal with laser and inkjet office printers.

slides.title: What happens in those steps
bullets: Charging: the drum gets a uniform charge.
Exposing: the laser writes the image.
Developing: toner sticks to the image.
Fusing: heat bonds the toner to the paper.
slides.narration: Here's the short version. After the page is processed in memory, the drum gets a uniform charge. The laser then exposes, or writes, the image onto the drum. Toner develops onto those areas, transfers to the paper, and finally the fuser uses heat and pressure to bond it permanently. Then the drum is cleaned, ready for the next page.

For network printers, knowing the I P address lets you add or manage it directly.

In PowerShell, run Get dash Printer to list printers, and Get dash Print Job to see what's waiting in the queue.

slides.title: Common issues
bullets: Paper jam: power off, remove paper gently.
Streaks or faded print: low toner or dirty drum.
Offline printer: check cable, Wi-Fi, or I P.
Stuck queue: clear jobs and restart the spooler.
slides.narration: Now the everyday faults. For a paper jam, power off and gently remove the paper in the direction it was travelling. Streaks or faded print usually mean low or faulty toner, or a dirty drum. An offline printer means Windows can't reach it, so check the cable, Wi-Fi, or I P address. And a stuck queue, where nothing prints, is fixed by clearing the jobs and restarting the spooler.

slides.title: Fixing a stuck print queue
bullets: Clear the waiting jobs first.
Restart the Spooler service.
Then try printing a test page.
One of the most common helpdesk fixes.
slides.narration: Here's the fix you'll use constantly. First clear the waiting jobs by piping Get dash Print Job into Remove dash Print Job. Then restart the spooler with Restart dash Service dash Name Spooler. Spooler is spelled S P O O L E R. After that, send a test page. This single sequence solves a huge share of printing tickets.
